title: Subdomain entry
description: One claim per file in domains/. The filename is the name, so domains/jane.is-a.ceo.json claims jane.is-a.ceo.

$schema.description: Editor hint. Point it at ../registry/schema.json for autocomplete.

owner.description: Who holds the name. Give at least one of username or email; id is optional.

username.description: GitHub handle. Ties the claim to the account that opens the pull request.

email.description: Address a maintainer can reach you at.

id.description: Numeric GitHub account id, from https://api.github.com/users/<username>. Optional; survives a rename.

repo.description: github.com/you/project, or a full https URL. Shown on the site.

description.description: One line, shown on the site.

proxied.description: Route A, AAAA and CNAME through the Cloudflare proxy. Leave it false for GitHub Pages, where proxying breaks certificate issuance.

records.description: Omit the key entirely for the GitHub Pages default. An empty object is treated the same way.

A.description: Public IPv4 addresses. A single address may be written as a bare string.

AAAA.description: Public IPv6 addresses. A single address may be written as a bare string.

CNAME.description: One target, as a bare string or a one-item array. Cannot share a name with A, AAAA, MX, NS, SRV or PTR, and cannot sit on the apex.

TXT.description: SPF, DMARC and provider verifications. A file named _<label>.<name>.<zone>.json has its TXT mirrored to _<label>.<zone> on publish, which is how a Vercel proof reaches the zone root.

MX.description: A bare hostname is accepted and gets priority 10.

SRV.description: priority, weight and port default to 0 when left out.
